subject.title: feat(cli): add openclaw agent exec headless one-shot runner

question: Should OpenClaw ship a core `agent exec` command whose default isolated policy disables the agent sandbox and permits full host execution for CI and coding automation?
rationale: The implementation deliberately establishes a new public automation contract and execution-security boundary; tests can validate mechanics but cannot decide the acceptable default trust model, support commitment, or whether this belongs in core.

options.title: Approve the isolated core runner
options.body: Accept the Gateway-free core command after maintainers confirm the privileged-host threat model and the contributor supplies redacted live success plus failure or timeout proof.

options.title: Require a narrower execution policy
options.body: Keep the feature direction but require sandboxed or explicitly opt-in host execution before exposing it as the default headless command.

options.title: Route the workflow outside core
options.body: Decline the new core execution surface and direct automation users to an existing supported integration or extension path if that better fits product scope.

recommendation.title: Approve the isolated core runner
recommendation.body: Accept the Gateway-free core command after maintainers confirm the privileged-host threat model and the contributor supplies redacted live success plus failure or timeout proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied PR history and assignment make steipete the best available routing candidate for clarifying the intended execution contract, subject to final maintainer approval.
